title: Mirror and Curtains
subtitle: A mirror, a razor in green, and hands reaching into nothingness.

trails.title: Surveillance Report on Ms. Weyerhaeuser
trails.description: About that forest you're familiar with. About that companion you know so well.

content.text:
Following the forest incident, Ms. Weyerhaeuser, suspected of using her arcane skills to destroy and invade on public places, and thus causing severe damage, was required to eliminate the influence of arcanum and restore the original function of the site, and was forced to participate in one hundred and twenty hours of Foundation service activities, in addition to a fine of two hundred thousand Sharpodonties.

    Ms. Weyerhaeuser showed a high degree of cooperation in accepting her punishment. She enrolled in the Temporary Tree Processing class and, within three days, dealt with the excessive tree overgrowth she had caused by trimming all the greenery within the Foundation—at her impassioned request, the materials from the processed trees will be fully utilized. In the following period, the Tree Processing Class responded to this request—we processed the trees into lumber and sent them to the engineering department. The by-products were processed into organic fertilizer, and the remaining fruits were distributed by the canteen at lunchtime to offset Ms. Weyerhaeuser's service activity time—the acorn bread and berry pies received quite good reviews.

    In summary, given Ms. Weyerhaeuser's excellent performance and good attitude in admitting her mistakes during this period, we believe she has fulfilled her compensatory obligations to our satisfaction, and it is recommended that surveillance and movement restrictions are lifted from Ms. Weyerhaeuser in advance. That is all.

trails.title: The Last Big Newsflash!
trails.description: Half of this newspaper page has been soaked in murky oil paint. Fortunately, the other half of the text is still faintly legible.

content.text:
I don't know if I'm crazy, maybe today is the end of the world, but I have to write this down—this is my duty as a journalist!

    The whole of Vienna has become an oil painting splashed with turpentine, and I'm not using that as a metaphor—literally!

    Everything is dripping with paint, and I'm no exception! Fortunately, my right hand is fine for now and I can still write.

    I thought three men fighting to the death over the pronunciation of a word would be enough to make the front page of the newspapers, but I was wrong—▊▊▊, a great war is unfolding! A great war that will involve the whole world! Those feet marching on the streets can't wait to throw the world into the roasting flames of hell! Hungarians, Austrians, Transleithanians, Germans, Cisleithanians, the streets and cafés are full of lunatics talking nonsense, except for me and the little girl who just came to make a phone call carrying a case of books. The girl was crying so sadly when she made the call, she ran so fast when she came that she even slipped and fell, and she didn't realize her books had fallen all over the place until after she finished the call. I don't understand what there is to cry about when everything has become like this everywhere, and any semblance of order will soon disappear. If there is anything that still makes you sad, then you should do everything in your power to destroy it, just like the editor who keeps rejecting my drafts—if I don't take him down, I'll never have my chance to shine.

    This article will appear in tomorrow's paper, along with the destruction of my editor, if the world hasn't ended by then.

items.text: Mirror and Curtains

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I never thought it would be the Timekeeper and the Apeiron arcanists who'd solve the problem. But now, even humans can cast this ritual.
Laplace is now in a rare state of tranquility, for the researchers have done all they can; there's nothing left for them to do.
With only 4 hours to go, this is the final calm before the "Storm."

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Indeed. The knot is the physical form of the ritual we were looking for. Surprisingly, the numerical code yielded practical results.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I thought it was necessary to report this to the Timekeeper's organization. It was her contribution.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But it did not go well.

items.speaker: Attendee
items.text: Forgive the interruption. What's a knot?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I will be glad to answer your question.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Knot theory is a branch of algebraic topology. In mathematics, a knot refers to a connected closed curve in three-dimensional Euclidean space that does not intersect itself. They can also be described as shapes in three-dimensional space that are homeomorphic to circles.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Knot theory focuses on the entanglement and configurations of closed curves in three-dimensional space, rather than the curves themselves. Since all closed curves are homeomorphic to circles, they can all be topologically categorized as circles.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: A knot equivalent to a two-dimensional circle is called an unknot. And ...

items.speaker: Attendee
items.text: I don't mean to question Laplace's expertise, but this approach may not be the best solution for widespread implementation.

items.speaker: Attendee
items.text: The concepts are complex even for us, let alone others. We can't expect to give an advanced math lesson to every individual under these circumstances.

items.speaker: Attendee
items.text: Doing math before the "Storm"—nobody's got time for that!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: As it turned out, presenting a technical report was much too premature. We should have a complete and official report once the immunity gear is produced.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Maybe you can change your approach the next time you report to the Foundation.
The robot shakes her head, disappointed by the failure of her report and the listener's math level.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I simply gave them honest answers.
She turns her head and looks thoughtfully out the window.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But, this solution is deserving of widespread implementation.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: All we need is a piece of rope, and tie it end to end.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And spend three to five minutes to make this knot.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This can be done anywhere, at any time, by anyone using any type of cordage.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The oldest, fastest, and most basic ritual, the key to braving the "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: ... is a knot.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Why didn't you tell the House of Integratus? I'm sure they would've funded us generously.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I will make sure to put it in my interdepartmental report.
A rare hint of frustration flickers across her face.
But she quickly moves on to a subject that deserves her attention.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But at this point in time, the knot only functions like an incantation.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is not suitable for widespread use until the research on the side effects and the converter are complete.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: In any case, I've completed all the tasks you assigned me.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: My last plea is, please never put Ulrich and I on the same team again.
The researcher lets out a deep yawn, feeling as if he hasn't slept in ages.
Maybe he can catch a quick nap before the final battle begins.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hm. I'm surprised that you're not in the lab. Something bothering you?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Wait, don't tell me you're charging here?
The robot turns to him, an approving smile on her face.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Excellent job, Researcher Adler. You have proven that you are keeping the locations of public outlets in Laplace in mind,

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: which is a positive sign for your resocialization.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But I am powering up to reach my optimal condition, preparing for what is to come—

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The scroll of Apeiron, the final piece of the puzzle, the key to minimizing any negative effects caused by the incantation.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Whoa! The designers on Artificial Somnambulism could use some of this inspiration.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Look at the clouds, painted with a syndrome of colors and interrupted by a glorious streak of rainbow. It's truly a masterpiece!
The red blur streaks forward at lightning speed, but the Olitiaus are still in hot pursuit.
Their skins are becoming increasingly vibrant due to the Storm Syndrome.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Funny. They're flying towards the headquarters out of instinct. Maybe they can sense immunity zones?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: These little beasts would make for a good study.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But I'm not in the mood to take any prisoners.
Lilya speeds up again, trying to lose the pursuers that are swarming behind her like a dark vortex.
In front of her, under the clouds, the gray buildings of the Foundation are now clearly visible.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Fuel and ammunition are running out.
Her altitude is low enough. She can almost see the hallway outside the committee room.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Heh. Maybe I should storm the vice president's office with them? But other people might get hurt there. Never mind.
She makes an abrupt turn, her mind racing with ideas.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Dive into the lake? But the splash might wet the scroll.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Wait, isn't that ...
Sprouts from the forest. That looks like a signal to land.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Ms. Lilya, this way!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ha. Good timing!
Her friend's presence has given her a clear sense of direction.
Without a second thought, she charges into the new forest with the huge herd in hot pursuit.
Just before crashing into the trees, Red 38 changes course and rockets upward in a perfectly straight line.
But the creatures behind her have no such finesse.
One by one, they slam into the mesh woven by the dense tangle of trees and vines.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff II
items.text: Enemies intercepted. Ally landed successfully.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff II
items.text: Ms. Druvis, the Olitiaus are all ensnared in vines!
The druid closes her eyes, savoring the fresh air.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: The winds of triumph sweep through the woods. An excellent flight, Ms. Lilya.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: We will take it from here. Come, everyone, we shall vanquish our foes with the aid of the woods.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The special operations squad is ready to go.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Dr. Kakania, are you really going to stay here?
She shakes her head, her fingers tight on Marcus's communicator.
For more than ten hours, she has been waiting for Laplace to respond.
Marcus lowers her eyes, burying her face in her scarf to hide the tears.
The doctor quickly notices it, her voice softens and changes to a lighter tone.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't worry about me, young missy. This won't be goodbye forever.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Besides, I have already provided all the help I can, right?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I made Isolde show us the ritual and kept her under control. And now you've figured out how the ritual works.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: To test its results, you will need a couple of volunteers.
But Marcus doesn't seem to find comfort in her words.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But you heard the report from Laplace: the possibility of surviving the ritual is nearly zero without a converter and the scroll ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Nearly, they said, but not surely.
The doctor interjects briskly.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Plus, where else can I go?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I was born and raised in this city. This is where I came from, where I lived, and where I belong. This is my whole world.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I despised the maggots under its golden surface, and fought for the justice and fairness in our society. But I also cherish every detail of this city, from the intricate carvings on the theater columns, to the dirt trodden by dock workers.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: All of these things made me me—my family, my friends, my people, and my operas and culture, are all here.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I never once thought about leaving this place.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I have never thought about destroying it, either.
She looks up and sighs sentimentally.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Being washed away with it would be a just punishment for all my sins.
Yet her eyes are free of darkness and despair.
Marcus can clearly see her determination.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I wish I could be as brave as you are.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: See you, Ms. Klara.
She gently reaches out to her.
Not far away, the special operations squad is ready to go.
The helicopter begins to whirl. Its last errand of the day.
Inside the cabin, Isolde sits between two "Razor" operatives, her wrists bound in cuffs.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Hurry, ladies! Before any of us turns into one of those exquisite paintings.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Sorry, but the headquarters is too far for the teleportation disk from here. You'll have to bear with us smelly old grunts for a little longer.
It is time to part ways.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Goodbye, Ms. Marcus.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sharing this era with you has been an honor.
Their warm hands clasp in a powerful handshake.
With a wave to the teary-eyed girl, Kakania turns around and heads toward the city of madness.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Is your birthday approaching, doctor?
She twirls sharply around at the entranced voice.
Isolde reaches out into the air, still in a dream she's unwilling to wake up from.
There, the world is unchanged, and each day is filled with bliss.
For a prisoner in the Foundation's facility, perhaps dreams will provide the solace she needs.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I made this for you.
She holds out a brooch. A piece so exquisite that it, too, seems to be an intangible figment of a wistful dream.
The golden setting nestles the sparkling gem in place, a gift undoubtedly made with great affection.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Turquoise and Topaz, just like you and your eyes.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Please accept my blessings, doctor. May your life be filled with joy and contentment, and may your courage guide you through all that comes your way.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You are worthy of all the beauty and goodness this world has to offer, and I will hold you in my heart and in my prayers, forever.
Today isn't Kakania's birthday, nor can she see her reflection in Isolde's lusterless eyes.
The Star of Vienna holds up the brooch, yearning at the emptiness before her.
If one were to die today ...
What would she say to her long-time friend?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sweet dreams, Ms. Dittarsdorf.
She takes the brooch and pins it to her jacket.
The communicator at her waist crackles.
A ray of hope shines through the static.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Madam Lucy! Any progress on the research?
TO BE CONTINUED…
